body: Alaska's most common license plate is all yellow, but a large orange circle design appears in Generation 4. Front plates are required.
The Alaskan highway shield features the Big Dipper constellation on the bottom left.
Trees in Alaska are typically thinner with less broad leaves compared to other US states.
Tall, snow-covered mountains are a frequent sight in Alaskan Street View coverage.
Unlike most of the US, Alaska has a significant amount of Generation 2 coverage.
Alaska features "smallcam" Generation 4 coverage, which is lower-mounted with a wide circular blur and a visible white car front. The blur can sometimes be transparent.
Alaska is the only US state with prevalent shitcam coverage, characterized by low resolution, faded colors, and a large blur at the bottom.
This map displays the Street View coverage in Alaska, indicating the camera generation used for each road.
Generation 4 coverage in Alaska is mainly concentrated around the city of Anchorage.
Interior and northern Alaska are in subarctic or tundra climates, with little forest undergrowth and shorter trees.

Towns in Alaska's Alexander Archipelago have a unique look with tall mountains, lush green forests, and wooden buildings. The Generation 2 coverage is often overcast and misty, which can look similar to coastal Oregon and Washington.
The only major urban areas in Alaska are Anchorage and Fairbanks.
Most suburban areas are around Anchorage, with wide roads and distant mountains. Fairbanks has similar areas but with less prominent mountains.
Aspen trees, identifiable by their white bark and rounded leaves, are found in lower elevations of interior and south-central Alaska.
Due to the cold climate, agricultural fields in Alaska are mainly located in the south, particularly in the Matanuska Valley and Kenai Peninsula.
The Alaskan pipeline is often visible from main roads and is a unique feature for identifying Alaska within the US.
Juneau, the capital, is the largest and most 'built up' settlement in the Alaskan panhandle, surrounded by heavily forested mountains.
Fire hydrants in Anchorage are typically pale pink or pale yellow.
Fairbanks fire hydrants are commonly bright yellow or a combination of colours, most often yellow and blue.
Shitcam coverage is exclusive to the areas around Anchorage and Fairbanks and the road connecting them. The provided map shows all locations, but coverage might be updated.
The northern end of the Dalton Highway has a flat, snowy landscape under an overcast sky, with a small ridge of hills occasionally visible to the west.
The Denali Highway is a mostly gravel, east-west road in the 'Alaska' mountain range covered in Generation 2. It features wildflowers and green shrubs from its late summer coverage.
The Steese Highway is another east-west gravel road with Generation 2 coverage, but with noticeably lower mountains than the Denali Highway.
Highway 5 near the Yukon border is known for its foggy, rainy weather and Generation 2 camera. Unlike the similar Canadian highway, the American side is partly gravel and has outer lines where paved.
Prudhoe Bay, the northernmost covered town, is identified by its cold, dead landscape, overcast sky, and lack of tall buildings. A second Google car might be visible.

The isolated towns of Nome, Unalakleet, and Galena are covered only by a trekker, recognizable by a lime green hat or a black and white beanie. A black and white bandana is unique to the Nome trekker.
